anya-support: Escalation - customer report: intermittent INVALID_JSON when using structured output (json_mode) with session reuse. Ticket INC-9876. Happens after ~25-40 calls in same session, some responses contain merged JSON fragments from prior prompts. Severity: high :rotating_light:

customer-jc: Pasting a real response we got (customer redacted):
```json
{"id": 42, "user": {"id": "u-1", "name": "Alice"}, "items": [ {"type":"A","v":1}, {"type":"B","v":2} ], "meta": {"req_id":"abc123"}}
# but sometimes we get:
{"id": 42, "user": {"id": "u-1", "name": "Alice"}, "items": [ {"type":"A","v":1}, {"type":"B","v":2} ], "meta": {"req_id":"abc123"}},{"id": 43, "user": {"id": "u-2", "name": "Bob"}, "items": [ {"type":"C","v":3} ]}
```
The trailing comma + second object breaks JSON.parse on customer side.

anya-support: Repro details from customer:
- using model: redwood-1-large (hosted)
- endpoint: /v1/generate (json_mode: true, session_id: "cust-sess-71")
- client uses streaming=false, but we enable prefix cache=true and batching=true
- rate: bursts of 30 req/min
- attached curl they used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","json_mode":true,"session_id":"cust-sess-71","prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'
```

samir-eng-runtime: Thanks. Can you share the trace_id + any request_ids? Is this only with cache enabled? Also is tenant on Dedicated or Hosted?

anya-support: trace_id: tx-0a1b2c3d, sample req_ids: [r-9001, r-9002, r-9003]. Customer is on Hosted (paid plan). Repro note: when they disable prefix cache, the issue seems to go away in quick tests. Also seeing occasional 504/latency spikes before corrupted responses.

lee-ml: Quick hypothesis: frame boundary race between batcher and prefix/KV cache replay. If two requests share the same session prefix and batch window merges output frames without proper frame headers, you can get concatenated JSON chunks. Looks like a missing frame delimiter or non-atomic append to output buffer.

samir-eng-runtime: I'm going to reproduce locally against a backed pool with cache + batching enabled. Can infra fetch logs for tx-0a1b2c3d and the worker that handled r-9002?

infra-bot: Logs exported: https://logs.internal/redwood/tx-0a1b2c3d (expires in 7d). Worker id: w-42. Attached quick dump: `out_buffer` shows two writes within same millisecond without sequence header.

samir-eng-runtime: I reproduced with a small load generator that sends overlapping session requests. Reproducer: toggled stream framing off -> still reproduced. Looks like when batcher flushes multiple continuations for same session, the code writes frames back-to-back: e.g. `...}{...` instead of `...}

` (missing newline/sep). Patch idea: ensure every write includes explicit frame boundary token and make buffer append atomic per-request. I'll open a PR with a mutex guard around output serialization and add sequence ids in frame metadata.

anya-support: Customer asks about PII cross-tenant leakage. From samples they gave, it seems like structural merge, not content from other tenants. Can you confirm no user data from other customers leaked?

lee-ml: Quick scan of the logs for w-42: merged fragments are from same tenant session_id (cust-sess-71), no tokens from other tenant ids. Not a cross-tenant content leak, this appears to be frame coalescing. Still high-priority since it breaks JSON parsing.

paul-sre: Proposed mitigations: 1) tenant-level feature flag to disable prefix cache for the affected customer (fast). 2) schedule rolling restart of affected serving pool at 23:00 UTC to clear any inconsistent state. 3) apply runtime patch to ensure atomic writes and extra frame markers. I'll coordinate canary rollouts.

samir-eng-runtime: Opening PR + issue: runtime#1423 -> references INC-9876 and includes extra trace instrumentation (frame_seq_id, request_id) and a failing unit test for edge case. Will add canary gate.

anya-support: I'll notify customer with temporary mitigation (disable prefix cache) and ETA for fix. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

customer-jc: Appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted on timeline.

samir-eng-runtime: Setting target: patch rolled to canary within 8 hours, full rollout after validation. Will update INC-9876 with progress and reproduction artifacts.

anya-support: Closing loop: I'll update ticket and follow up after canary. If customer sees any additional corrupt responses, request they include `trace_id` and exact `session_id` so we can map them.
